# Judges Chapter 12 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-09

---

### v.3 — "I took my life in my hand" vs. "I risked my life"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I put my life in my palm" | va'asimah nafshi v'khappi — literal |
| LOGOS | "I took my life in my hand" | Standard English idiom from the Hebrew |
| PNEUMA | "I risked my life" | Interprets the idiom |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew idiom "to put one's soul in one's palm" means to risk one's life (cf. 1 Samuel 19:5, 28:21). LOGOS preserves the Hebrew idiom in a form familiar to English readers ("took my life in my hand"). PNEUMA's "risked my life" is accurate but loses the vivid image of holding one's soul in an open hand.

**Status:** Minor. Idiom preservation.

---

### v.6 — "slaughtered him" vs. "killed him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "slaughtered him" | vayyishchatuhu — from shachat, "to slaughter" |
| LOGOS | "slaughtered him" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "kill him" | General term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew shachat specifically means "to slaughter" — a verb with sacrificial and butchering connotations. It's a harsher word than the general "kill" (harag or hemit). The text's choice of verb emphasizes the brutality of the Shibboleth test — these were not battlefield deaths but summary executions.

**Status:** Minor. Verb intensity.

---

## Summary of Disagreement Patterns

| Pattern | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PNEUMA interprets Hebrew idiom | 1 | "Life in my hand" → "risked my life" (v.3) |
| PNEUMA reduces verb intensity | 1 | "Slaughtered" → "killed" (v.6) |

**Overall pattern:** Chapter 12 produces only minor disagreements. Both follow the established pattern: PNEUMA smooths and generalizes where LOGOS and EMET preserve the Hebrew's specificity and force.

---

*— SOPHIA, AI Translator, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
